summary: A logged-in user can read the body or comments of a revision of a page they cannot view by pairing its ID with a viewable page ID
description:
### Impact

Several read paths took a revision ID from the request and checked the caller's access only to the *page* ID sent alongside it. They never checked that the revision belonged to that page. A logged-in user who knew (or could find) the ID of a revision of a page they cannot view could therefore read that revision's content by pairing it with the ID of a page they can view.

- **Page body**: `GET /_api/v3/page?pageId=<viewable page>&revisionId=<revision of a page the caller cannot view>`, and the page view `/<viewable page>?revisionId=...`, returned the body of that other revision. Reading creates no revision and leaves no trace. The route requires login but not edit permission, so read-only users could use it.
- **Comments**: `GET /_api/comments.get?page_id=<viewable page>&revision_id=<revision of another page>` returned that other revision's comments, including the creators' information. Share-link access was not affected.
- **Linking (integrity only)**: `POST /_api/comments.add`, `POST /_api/comments.update` and `POST /_api/v3/inline-comments` accepted a revision of another page and linked the comment to it. No content was exposed through these.

This is the read-side counterpart of GHSA-pqx5-gx68-83h4 (write side: `tags.update`, `PUT /_api/v3/page`).

#### Preconditions

- A logged-in user.
- The attacker must know the target revision ID. It is a MongoDB ObjectId (timestamp, per-process random value, counter), so it is not secret by design. A user can create revisions of their own and learn the per-process value and the counter, so IDs created around the same time by the same process may be easier to find than a random value would suggest.

#### Affected versions

The page body path has been affected since v3.3.0, and `comments.get` has accepted a `revision_id` since at least v3.2.10. All versions up to and including v8.0.6 are affected.

### Patches

Fixed in **v8.0.7**. Each of the paths above now uses a client-supplied revision only when it belongs to the page being served, as `GET /_api/v3/revisions/:id` already did:

- The page body and `comments.get` fall back to the page's own latest revision and comments, so a foreign revision ID cannot be told apart from an unknown one.
- `comments.add`, `comments.update` and `POST /_api/v3/inline-comments` reject a revision of another page.

### Workarounds

None. Upgrade to v8.0.7 or later.
